title: Roles and access restrictions
goal: Test object and row-level restrictions with negative cases without broadening permissions.
prerequisites: onec.p9; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.
outcomes: Test object and row-level restrictions with negative cases without broadening permissions.
sections: A role permits object operations; data restrictions refine scope. A user allowedAlpha requests does not gainBeta access merely by knowing a key. Test lists, direct open and edits. Hidden buttons and editable client filters are not authorization enforcement.

Engineering quality follows invariants, not absence of exceptions. Balance uses admissible amounts, permissions authorized scope, diagnostics explainable failure without leaks. Specify what survives errors and concurrent actions. Positive cases prove utility; negative cases prove boundaries. Denying everything is not a universally correct security implementation. Evidence needs both operational success and correctly bounded rejection.

Additional roles change effective permissions. Analyze the full set and context, not one role alone. Full rights can hide missing enforcement. Use separate synthetic least-privilege profiles and a positive control so a denial is not merely an inability to log in.

Transactions, locks and authorization solve different problems. Atomicity coordinates one operation, locking interacting operations, and rights constrain subjects. None proves the others. Identify decision point, read data and authorized actor for each failure scenario. Choose minimal protection rather than enabling every capability or broadening privileges. A context compile check is not a multi-user access proof.

Privileged execution can alter normal permission boundaries. Do not enable it merely to silence a read error; justify need and outputs. Even aggregates can disclose forbidden information. Agree on a minimal contract and test indirect routes as well as visible records.

Measurement/observability must preserve privacy. Use synthetic IDs, bounded logs and defined metrics. Passwords/tokens are unnecessary even for leak demonstrations; use canaries. One timing is not p95, and one profile result does not cover every role/configuration combination. Keep raw diagnostics restricted and publish only sufficient sanitized evidence tied to the actual test environment.
Bind the matrix to the actual environment

Record build, profile, object, action, scope and expectation. TestAlpha, Beta, direct references, writes and aggregates in a suitable stand. Mark unavailable training checksNOTRUN. Logs contain no passwords or full user data; successful login is not a complete security audit.

Security acceptance needs discriminating tests in a permitted environment. Races need two controlled sessions, roles allowed work plus bypass attempts, and isolation denial of a specific resource. Preserve traces/post-failure state and repeat a successful control. Unsupported environments yieldNOTRUN; static analysis or diagrams cannot automatically fill that evidence gap. Report the remaining gate explicitly.
